subject: Polity
description: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, law-making process, privileges, procedures

questions.stem: The TERM of a Lok Sabha member is normally:
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha = 5-year term (unless dissolved earlier). Rajya Sabha members serve 6-year terms; one-third retire every 2 years (permanent body).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The maximum strength of Lok Sabha as per the Constitution is:
questions.explanation: Post the 104th Amendment (2020): maximum 550 members — up to 530 from States + up to 20 from Union Territories. The Anglo-Indian nominated seats (2) were abolished by the 104th Amendment. Current strength is 543 elected.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The SPEAKER of the Lok Sabha is elected:

options.option_text: By members of the Lok Sabha from amongst themselves
By joint sitting of both houses

questions.explanation: Article 93: Lok Sabha 'shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker'. The Speaker presides over the House, decides on Money-Bill certification, maintains order. Pro-tem Speaker (usually senior-most MP) administers oath to newly-elected members before regular Speaker is chosen.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: A MONEY BILL can be introduced in:

options.option_text: Either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
Only Lok Sabha, on the recommendation of the President
Any House, but only with the consent of the Prime Minister

questions.explanation: Article 109: Money Bills (Art 110) originate only in Lok Sabha, with prior recommendation of the President. Rajya Sabha must return within 14 days and can only make recommendations (which Lok Sabha may accept or reject). The Speaker certifies a Bill as Money Bill — and his decision is final.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The JOINT SITTING of both houses of Parliament is convened by the President under:
questions.explanation: Article 108 — President may summon joint sitting in case of deadlock on a non-money bill. The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides. Only 4 joint sittings have been held: Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill (1978), Election Laws Amendment Bill (2002 — POTA), and no further since.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The QUORUM to constitute a meeting of either house of Parliament is:
questions.explanation: Article 100(3) — minimum of 1/10 of the total members of the House. For Lok Sabha (543), quorum = 55. For Rajya Sabha (~245), quorum = 25.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Consider the following about the RAJYA SABHA. 1. It is a permanent body — not subject to dissolution. 2. Maximum strength is 250: 238 elected + 12 nominated by the President. 3. Members are elected by single transferable vote by MLAs of state legislatures. 4. Nominated members are chosen for outstanding contribution in literature, science, art, or social service. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Rajya Sabha = Council of States. UT members (Delhi and Puducherry) are elected by their respective legislative assemblies. Nominated members cannot vote in Presidential elections.
questions.subject: Polity
